correctness.rationale: All type marginals remain exactly one half for every b, so the incoming global-contact type is uniform; for size-two households a partner is locally infected with \(p_{ij}=1-e^{-\lambda_{ij}}\), and global household offspring are conditionally Poisson with mean \( eta_i\) or \( eta_i+ eta_j\). Exact fractions yield the displayed PGF mixtures; derivative means \(7/2\) and \(801/200\). Since \(e^{4/5}>53/25>2\), the two exact coefficient evaluations at \(u=1/2\), \(30049/204800\) and \(2159/12800\), are below \(1/5\), enclosing every extinction root. On this interval the difference polynomial is at least \(3839/512>0\), forcing strict ordering of unique nontrivial fixed points, hence opposite monotonicities of mean and takeoff probability. Uniform margins and compact parameter dependence prove robust persistence. The provided standalone checker recomputes all exact inequalities; supplementary Theorem 9.1 independently supplies the underlying large-population branching approximation, not any mathematical novelty certification. Computations are algebraic, not evidence of infinite limits by enumeration.

originality.rationale: The general household PGF and extinction limit are known, as is qualitative failure of ordering epidemics by the household reproduction number (Ball–Sirl–Trapman 2010, Fig. 7, as cited by Ball–Critcher 2026 and Britton–Pardoux 2019). The narrower, explicit claim compared here is a strict opposite ordering for **every** within-type/heterotypic pair-matching fraction with fixed type marginals and fixed six biological parameters, plus perturbative robustness, inside the 2026 proportionate-global-mixing model. Neither the inspected source main text and supplement nor the relevant 2011 global-assortative and 2025 homogeneous-household perturbation claims implies this pointwise family. published-finding corpus comparisons retrieved none with this claim, although absence from search is not novelty proof. Related inaccessible 2010 full text leaves specified residual risk.
residual_risks: The full text of Ball–Sirl–Trapman (2010), especially Figure 7, was not obtainable from the open sources examined. The already-known qualitative warning has been excluded from the new claim. A finer comparison with that full article remains a documented risk.

value.rationale: The exact invariant problem is the pair-matching interpolation between same-type and cross-type household configurations under fixed type frequencies and fixed person-level infection laws. R* is routinely used to compare structured epidemics, but only acts as an existence threshold; this explicit theorem establishes a sharp full-interval failure of risk ranking, not just one numerical pair, and proves it persists under small biological parameter errors. The mismatch has an identified structural mechanism: reallocating local secondary infections changes both the expected number of high-infectivity infected individuals and offspring dispersion. The qualitative phenomenon was known and is not presented as new. Exact fixed-marginal monotonicity in the recent two-type model is mathematically useful as a robust benchmark for assessing whether a scalar reproduction summary preserves the ranking of outbreak risks. No empirical outbreak, public-health prescription, final-size ranking or general all-model theorem is asserted.
